title: Inherent Trade-Offs between Diversity and Stability in Multi-Task Benchmarks
reasoning: The paper uses social choice theory to evaluate the mathematical stability and diversity of existing multi-task benchmarks (including those related to fairness and alignment). It does not conduct its own evaluation or benchmarking of religion, faith, morals, or ethics as its primary focus; rather, it treats those topics' benchmarks as generic task aggregations for its theoretical meta-analysis.
